title: Do you interpret films to be in their own universe?

commenti.body:
I don't really understand what you're asking. 

I mean, to the question in your title: yes. We understand any given film to possess and be bounded by a world. That world will be more or less similar to our world in all sorts of ways: everything from history and culture to physics and visual appearances. Generally fiction will be more-or-less different, whereas we accept that the world of a documentary is isomorphic with our world.

Crucially, though, not even in the case of a documentary is the world the Same as ours. If I speak to a character on a screen they will not, cannot, hear me. Nor can I smell the food they are eating. Theirs is a world (the fancy term is "diegesis") separate from ours, which we can spy/eavesdrop on but have no direct access to.

So that's my answer to your question. But I'm sure what you're asking about audiences in the last 30 years?
